mainEntity.name: How much does an outdoor sauna cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the size, the heater and your site. Our best-selling Pure Cube 552 is $11,884. Delivery, the base and electrical work vary by property, so we give every customer a personalized quote after a consultation.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit for a backyard sauna?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your municipality. In Toronto, for example, a building permit is generally required for an accessory structure larger than 10 m² (107 sq ft), or one that's attached to your house or has plumbing. Electrical work must be done by a licensed electrician. We'll help you check your local rules before you buy.

mainEntity.name: Where do you deliver and install?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ontario and British Columbia. In the GTA we install in Toronto, Mississauga, Oakville, Burlington, Vaughan, Richmond Hill, Markham, Aurora, King and Whitby, and across Ontario from Niagara-on-the-Lake and Prince Edward County to Collingwood, Muskoka and Haliburton. Sauna delivery and installation is $1,750 anywhere in Ontario. We also install in British Columbia, and anywhere outside Ontario is quoted on request.

mainEntity.name: Can I use an outdoor sauna in a Canadian winter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely, winter is the best season for it. Our saunas are built from premium Canadian cedar and sized with heaters that bring them up to temperature year-round.

mainEntity.name: Do you build custom saunas?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We design custom outdoor saunas and indoor sauna rooms for homes, cottages and rentals. Tell us about your space and we'll come back with a design and quote.

mainEntity.name: How long does installation take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The installation itself usually takes about 5 to 6 hours on site. From the day you order to installation day is typically 2 to 4 weeks, and we confirm your date when you order.

mainEntity.name: What do I need to start with a new sauna?

acceptedAnswer.text: At minimum: a bucket and ladle for making steam, a thermometer and a sand timer. Our Starter package covers the bucket, ladle and thermometer and adds eucalyptus essence. The Deluxe and Supreme packages add a sand timer and backrests. Every package is 10% off the individual prices.

mainEntity.name: Do you deliver accessories across Ontario?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We ship accessories anywhere in Ontario; shipping is quoted by phone based on your order and location. If you are buying a sauna from us, we can bring your accessories with your sauna delivery and set them up on installation day.

mainEntity.name: Can I see the accessories before I buy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Visit our showroom at 17380 Highway 27, Schomberg, ON L0G 1T0. Visits are by appointment; call (437) 429-6623 to book.

mainEntity.name: What is your return policy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unused accessories in their original packaging can be returned. Processing fees and shipping costs are deducted from your refund. Contact us before sending anything back so we can arrange the return.

mainEntity.name: Which heater control do I need?

acceptedAnswer.text: HUUM electric heaters need a HUUM UKU control: choose Wi-Fi for app control or Local for an in-sauna panel only. Homecraft heaters run through a contactor and touchpad; pick the indoor or outdoor version to match where your sauna sits, and Wi-Fi if you want to start it from your phone.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a safety railing around my heater?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is not required, but we recommend one for families and for smaller saunas where knees and elbows are close to the heater. HUUM makes fitted railings for the Drop and HIVE Mini.

mainEntity.name: What accessories suit a barrel sauna?

acceptedAnswer.text: A curved ceiling heat shield above the heater, a cedar backrest or two, a floor mat, and a bucket, ladle and thermometer. Wood-fired barrels pair well with a cedar firewood barrel or a Narvi wood basket.

mainEntity.name: Are LED lights safe inside a sauna?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Every light we carry is made for sauna heat and humidity. The SaunaScapes Sade RGB sets and the Kaiku sound system carry a 2-year warranty, and the Electric Sauna Light is marine-grade.

mainEntity.name: What is soapstone, and why use it?

acceptedAnswer.text: A dense Finnish stone that absorbs heat slowly and releases it gently, which makes it ideal for steam stones, aroma cups and thermometers.

mainEntity.name: How do I look after the cedar?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use Meldos sauna oil on interior cedar and Livos oil on the exterior. Left untreated, cedar weathers to a silver-grey that many owners love.

mainEntity.name: What temperature should a cold plunge be?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most people find 10°C to 15°C (50°F to 59°F) the sweet spot. Experienced plungers sometimes go colder, and our chillers can reach 37°F (2.8°C).

mainEntity.name: Can I use a cold plunge outdoors in a Canadian winter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Cedar handles moisture and temperature swings well, and a cover helps. At 0°C (32°F) or below, either drain the tub or keep the chiller running so it doesn't freeze.

mainEntity.name: Do the tubs need plumbing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Fill with a garden hose and drain through the built-in drain. Chillers are self-contained and connect directly to the tub; their electrical connection must be made by a licensed electrician.

mainEntity.name: Stainless steel or HDPE?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Polar and Glacier come with either. 304 stainless steel is the premium, easy-clean option; HDPE is a durable, seamless liner at a lower price.

mainEntity.name: Is shower hardware included?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Every shower is sold as the cedar unit on its own, so you can use hardware you already have. Add our Premium Shower Hardware for a stainless rain head, hand shower and hot and cold mixing valve.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a plumber?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not for a cold rinse: the Sunlight, Sierra and Savannah connect to a standard garden hose. For hot and cold water through the premium hardware, a licensed plumber may be needed.

mainEntity.name: What about winter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drain the lines and hardware fully before freezing weather. The cedar can stay outside year-round; leave it to weather to silver-grey or keep the colour with an exterior oil.

mainEntity.name: Red cedar or white cedar?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Sunlight, Cloudburst, Rainbow Barrel and Skylight are Western red cedar, in knotty or clear grade. The Sierra and Savannah are Eastern White Cedar from the Canadian Timber Collection.

mainEntity.name: How do I know what size heater I need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Measure your sauna's length, width and height in feet and multiply them to get cubic feet, then pick a heater whose range covers that number. Add volume for glass walls or doors. Every heater page lists the room range for each kW output, or send us your measurements and we'll recommend one.

mainEntity.name: Electric or wood-burning: what's the difference?

acceptedAnswer.text: Electric heaters reach temperature in about 30 to 45 minutes, give you precise control, and need a dedicated 240V circuit. Wood-burning stoves take longer to heat, run off-grid, and bring the atmosphere of a real fire. Both make steam when you pour water on the stones.

mainEntity.name: How much is delivery for a heater?

acceptedAnswer.text: Delivery for a heater bought on its own is quoted for your location, or you can pick it up free at our Schomberg showroom when in stock. If you buy a sauna from us, the heater is included in the sauna's delivery and installation.

mainEntity.name: What size breaker does a sauna heater need?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the heater and its output: from a 30 A double-pole breaker for 6 kW heaters like the HUUM Drop 6 kW or Harvia KIP 6 kW, up to 80 A for the Homecraft Apex 15 kW. The exact breaker and wire size for every output is listed on each heater page.

mainEntity.name: Do I need an electrician and a permit in Ontario?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. An electric sauna heater must be connected by a licensed electrical contractor under an Electrical Safety Authority (ESA) permit, following the Ontario Electrical Safety Code.

mainEntity.name: Can I start my sauna from my phone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with a Wi-Fi control. HUUM heaters use the UKU Wi-Fi control, and Homecraft heaters can be paired with a Homecraft Wi-Fi touchpad. Both are available on our Accessories page.

mainEntity.name: Is there a difference between indoor and outdoor controls?

acceptedAnswer.text: For Homecraft heaters, yes: choose the outdoor contactor and touchpad for a backyard sauna, and the indoor version for a basement or home sauna.

mainEntity.name: Do wood-burning heaters need a chimney?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Wood-burning stoves need a chimney, installed to local building codes, on a non-combustible base with the clearances listed for each stove. Check your home insurer's requirements before installing a wood stove.

mainEntity.name: Are the electric heaters safety certified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Homecraft heaters (Revive, Revive Slim, Apex Mini and Apex) are CSA certified to UL 875, and the Harvia KIP is UL/cUL listed.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with each heater?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homecraft heaters carry a 2-year manufacturer warranty, HUUM heaters a 3-year warranty, the Harvia KIP up to 3 years, and Narvi stoves 2 years. Details are on each heater page.

mainEntity.name: Where are your heaters made?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homecraft (Revive, Revive Slim, Apex Mini, Apex) and TimberGlow are made in Canada. Narvi stoves and the Harvia KIP come from Finland. HUUM heaters are designed in Estonia, and the Pellum pellet stove is designed and made there too.
